## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 1v1 online round-based paintball FPS with diverse comeback upgrades and selectable match length and arena rotation.

## Requirements
- User requested an FPS 1v1 shooter with the losing player choosing a power-up after each round.
- Include plentiful, diverse movement, health, and weapon upgrades; paintball-style arenas with varied aesthetics; selectable number of rounds and maps per match.
- Build the game without clarification; briefly note assumptions when finishing.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser game using HTML canvas raycasting, with a bot opponent and a peer-to-peer WebRTC online option.
- Added four arenas and round-count options of 3, 5, 7, or 9.
- A losing player chooses one of three randomized upgrades; a winner keeps their current loadout.
- Match winner is based on the configured total rounds.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game lobby and arena setup UI in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Implemented canvas arena rendering, movement, aiming, paintball firing, bot opponent, rounds, scores, and upgrade selection in `game.js`.
- Added four visually distinct maps: Dusty Depot, Neon Yard, Jungle Run, and Frost Bite.
- Added 12 upgrade types, including speed, health, fire rate, damage, ammo, reload, projectile speed, slow, healing, spread, sprint, and radar.
- Added WebRTC peer connection offer/answer UI and game state exchange.
- Confirmed JavaScript parses with `node --check game.js`; opened the game in Playwright and verified lobby and gameplay render. Screenshots saved to `/tmp/opencode/splatter.jpg` and `/tmp/opencode/splatter-game.jpg`.

### Active
- Added directional movement-control buttons to `index.html` for mobile play, but their styling and input handling are not implemented yet.
- Online mode and round synchronization need further testing/fixes.

### Blocked
- Browser check reported only a missing `favicon.ico` (404), which does not affect gameplay.

## Next Move
1. Add styling for `.move-controls` and pointer/touch handlers mapping directional buttons to movement keys.
2. Test mobile layout and gameplay controls, then test the bot round loss/win and perk-pick flow.
3. Review/fix WebRTC peer handshake, player orientation/scoring synchronization, and online loss/win behavior.
4. Check for remaining gameplay/runtime defects and report assumptions briefly when done.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: lobby, setup controls, gameplay HUD, overlays, and mobile controls.
- `style.css`: lobby, arena HUD, responsive layout, and game visual styling.
- `game.js`: map data, game loop, canvas rendering, bot opponent, perk system, rounds, and WebRTC implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local preview was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright opened `http://localhost:3002`.
- The `.move-controls` HTML was added immediately before handoff; no corresponding style or event handling exists yet.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 1v1 round-based paintball FPS with online play, comeback upgrades, selectable match length, and arena rotation.

## Requirements
- The lower-scoring player chooses a power-up after each round.
- Include diverse movement, health, and weapon upgrades, varied paintball arenas, and selectable rounds and maps per match.
- Build without clarification and briefly note assumptions when finishing.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser game with canvas raycasting, a bot opponent, and WebRTC peer-to-peer multiplayer.
- Added four arenas, match lengths of 3, 5, 7, or 9 rounds, and 12 upgrade types.
- Round winners keep their loadout; the losing player picks from three randomized upgrades.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive lobby, match setup, HUD, arena rendering, movement, aiming, paintball firing, bot opponent, scoring, and upgrade selection.
- Added Dusty Depot, Neon Yard, Jungle Run, and Frost Bite.
- Added mobile directional, fire, and sprint controls with pointer hold/release handling.
- Fixed WebRTC signaling flow so the joining player generates an answer and the host applies it; the host sends match settings/start to the joining player.
- `node --check game.js` passes; browser verification confirmed lobby and gameplay render, and mobile controls appear at 390×844.

### Active
- Test WebRTC host/join start, player orientation, damage, scoring, and round synchronization.
- Test bot round outcomes and losing-player perk selection; review remaining gameplay/runtime defects.
- Consider online perk/loadout and round-state synchronization after exercising multiplayer.

### Blocked
- Browser automation reports a harmless `favicon.ico` 404; no gameplay impact.

## Next Move
1. Exercise host/join WebRTC handshake and verify both players start the same configured match.
2. Test online round results, score, progression, and perk-choice behavior; fix any synchronization defects.
3. Test bot match outcomes and perk flow, then recheck desktop and mobile controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Lobby, game HUD, overlays, online setup, and mobile controls.
- `style.css`: Game styling, responsive layout, and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Arenas, rendering, movement, bot, perks, rounds, and WebRTC implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the observed `git status`.
- Local preview is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright opened the preview and verified gameplay; screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/current-game.png`.
- The browser console’s only observed error was the missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
